question: Most of the Harappan sites are primarily divided into ________ parts.
solution:
The Correct answer is __**two**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Most of the **Harappan sites** are primarily divided into **two parts:** the **Citadel** and the **Lower Town.**
 
• The **Citadel** was a raised area, often fortified, where rulers or elites lived. It contained large structures such as granaries, assembly halls, and possibly religious buildings.
 
• The **Lower Town** was the larger area meant for common people. It included houses, workshops, streets, and other facilities.
 
• The division into two parts reflects the **planned urban layout** of Harappan cities, showcasing their advanced knowledge of **town planning, drainage systems, and architecture.**
 
• Examples of this division can be observed at sites like **Mohenjo-Daro, Harappa, and Dholavira.**
 
• The existence of a citadel highlights the presence of a **social hierarchy and administrative control** in Harappan civilization.
 
• The streets in Harappan cities were laid out in a **grid pattern**, with advanced drainage systems, indicating a high level of **civil engineering expertise.**
 
• The division also demonstrates the **importance of security** and the need to protect the elite and critical infrastructure from external threats or floods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Indus Valley Civilization

 
 
• The Indus Valley Civilization, also known as the Harappan Civilization, was one of the world's earliest urban civilizations, flourishing around 2500 BCE.
 
• It was characterized by well-planned cities, advanced drainage systems, and impressive architectural structures.
 
• Major sites include Harappa, Mohenjo-Daro, Dholavira, and Lothal.
 
 
 
• Harappan Trade
 
 
• Harappans engaged in extensive trade networks both within the Indian subcontinent and with distant lands like Mesopotamia, Persia, and the Arabian Peninsula.
 
• Goods traded included beads, pottery, cotton textiles, and precious stones.
 
 
 
• Harappan Architecture
 
 
• Harappan cities were known for their uniform grid patterns, with streets laid out in perfect right angles.
 
• Buildings were constructed using standardized baked bricks, and many structures featured intricate drainage systems.
 
 
 
• Archaeological Discoveries
 
 
• Excavations at Harappan sites have revealed a wealth of artifacts, including seals with inscriptions, weights and measures, and terracotta figurines.
 
• These discoveries provide valuable insights into the social, economic, and cultural aspects of the Harappan Civilization.
